title: Stock Futures Rise Ahead of Nvidia Earnings and Anthropic IPO: Live Market Updates – CNBC
body:
Wall Street opened the new week on a cautiously optimistic note, with major indices poised for another rally after posting their strongest weekly gains since August. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite each climbed more than 2 % over the past five trading days, buoyed by a surge in technology stocks and a broader risk‑on sentiment. Futures for all three benchmarks nudged higher on Sunday evening, signaling that investors are eager to build on the momentum while they await two marquee events: Nvidia’s earnings report and the anticipated initial public offering of artificial‑intelligence startup Anthropic.

The rally that lifted the market last week was driven largely by a rebound in mega‑cap tech names that had been under pressure after a series of earnings misses and heightened concerns about a tightening monetary environment. Nvidia, the chipmaker that has become the poster child for the AI boom, posted a staggering 13 % gain on Thursday, pulling the Nasdaq to a fresh record high. The company’s stock surged after it disclosed a revenue outlook that far outstripped analyst expectations, reinforcing the narrative that AI‑related hardware and software will dominate growth in the coming years. That surge helped lift the broader market, as investors reassessed the upside potential of other AI‑exposed firms.

Yet the optimism is tempered by the looming earnings release from Nvidia itself, scheduled for later this week. Analysts predict that the company will report a year‑over‑year revenue increase of more than 150 %, driven by soaring demand for its graphics processing units (GPUs) used in data‑center AI workloads. While the market has already priced in a strong performance, any deviation from the lofty forecasts could trigger a swift correction, especially given the sector’s recent volatility. Traders are also watching the company’s guidance on future chip supply, which could be constrained by ongoing semiconductor shortages and geopolitical tensions that affect the global supply chain.

Adding to the week’s intrigue is the expected debut of Anthropic, a San Francisco‑based AI startup founded by former OpenAI researchers. The company is slated to go public through a merger with a special‑purpose acquisition company (SPAC), a route that has become increasingly popular for high‑growth tech firms seeking faster market access. If successful, the IPO could become one of the largest AI‑focused listings to date, potentially raising upwards of $2 billion and providing a benchmark for how the market values pure‑play AI enterprises. Investors are keen to see how Anthropic’s valuation compares with rivals such as OpenAI’s backers and other AI chipmakers, as well as how the company’s product roadmap—centered on “constitutional AI” safety frameworks—will resonate with a broader audience.

Beyond the headline‑grabbing events, macroeconomic factors continue to shape market dynamics. The Federal Reserve’s latest policy meeting left interest rates unchanged, but officials signaled that further hikes remain on the table if inflation proves stubborn. That dovetail of steady rates and robust corporate earnings has helped sustain risk appetite, but any surprise in upcoming economic data—particularly on employment or consumer spending—could quickly shift sentiment. Moreover, the recent strengthening of the U.S. dollar has put pressure on multinational earnings, a factor that could weigh on sectors such as energy and materials even as tech leads the rally.

Looking ahead, the market’s trajectory will hinge on how Nvidia’s earnings and Anthropic’s IPO unfold, as well as the broader macro backdrop. Should Nvidia confirm its explosive growth and Anthropic achieve a strong debut, the AI theme could cement itself as the central driver of equity performance for the rest of the year. Conversely, any miss on earnings or a tepid IPO response may prompt investors to rotate back into more defensive holdings, tempering the recent surge. For now, the higher futures suggest that traders are ready to ride the wave, but they remain vigilant, aware that the next few days could set the tone for the market’s longer‑term direction.
